Constant.Label: pi

Function.Documentation: Computes the sine of an angle. The angle is interpreted using the current `#deg` / `#rad` / `#gra` setting; pass an angle with explicit units (`deg`, `rad`, `gra`) to override.
Computes the cosine of an angle. The angle is interpreted using the current `#deg` / `#rad` / `#gra` setting; pass an angle with explicit units to override.
Computes the tangent (sin/cos) of an angle. Undefined at odd multiples of π/2 (90°, 270°, ...).
Computes the cosecant (1/sin) of an angle. Undefined at integer multiples of π (0°, 180°, ...).
Computes the secant (1/cos) of an angle. Undefined at odd multiples of π/2 (90°, 270°, ...).
Computes the cotangent (cos/sin) of an angle. Undefined at integer multiples of π (0°, 180°, ...).
Returns the angle whose sine is `x`. Result is in the range [-π/2, π/2] (or [-90°, 90°]). Errors if |x| > 1.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Returns the angle whose cosine is `x`. Result is in the range [0, π] (or [0°, 180°]). Errors if |x| > 1.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Returns the angle whose tangent is `x`. Result is in the range (-π/2, π/2). For full-quadrant resolution from `(x, y)` coordinates, use `atan2`.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Returns the angle of the vector `(x, y)` measured from the positive x-axis, with the correct quadrant. Result is in (-π, π] (or (-180°, 180°]).
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Returns the angle whose cosecant is `x`. Defined for |x| ≥ 1.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Returns the angle whose secant is `x`. Defined for |x| ≥ 1.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Returns the angle whose cotangent is `x`.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Computes (e^x − e^-x) / 2. Argument is dimensionless.
Computes (e^x + e^-x) / 2. Argument is dimensionless. Result is always ≥ 1.
Computes sinh(x) / cosh(x). Result is in (-1, 1) and approaches ±1 for large |x|.
Computes 1 / sinh(x). Undefined at x = 0.
Computes 1 / cosh(x). Result is > 0 and ≤ 1.
Computes cosh(x) / sinh(x). Undefined at x = 0.
Returns the value whose hyperbolic sine is `x`. Equivalent to `ln(x + sqrt(x² + 1))`. Defined for all real `x`.
Returns the non-negative value whose hyperbolic cosine is `x`. Equivalent to `ln(x + sqrt(x² − 1))`. Errors if `x < 1`.
Returns the value whose hyperbolic tangent is `x`. Equivalent to `0.5 · ln((1 + x) / (1 − x))`. Errors if `|x| ≥ 1`.
Returns the value whose hyperbolic cosecant is `x`. Equivalent to `asinh(1/x)`. Undefined at `x = 0`.
Returns the value whose hyperbolic secant is `x`. Equivalent to `acosh(1/x)`. Defined for `x ∈ (0, 1]`.
Returns the value whose hyperbolic cotangent is `x`. Equivalent to `atanh(1/x)`. Defined for `|x| > 1`.
Computes log₁₀(x). Errors when `x ≤ 0` (real mode). For complex mode, the principal branch is used.
Computes the natural logarithm (base e) of `x`. Errors when `x ≤ 0` (real mode).
Computes log₂(x). Errors when `x ≤ 0` (real mode).
Computes Euler's number `e` raised to the power `x`. Inverse of `ln`.
Returns the principal square root of `x`. Identical to `sqrt`. Errors for negative `x` in real mode.
Function.Label: sqr(x)

Function.Documentation: Returns the principal square root of `x`. Identical to `sqr`. Errors for negative `x` in real mode.
Function.Label: sqrt(x)

Function.Documentation: Returns the real cube root of `x`. Defined for all real `x`, including negatives.
Returns the principal n-th root of `x`, equivalent to `x^(1/n)`. Use a positive integer for `n`.
Rounds `x` to the nearest integer using banker's rounding (ties go to even). Preserves units.
Returns the largest integer not exceeding `x`. Preserves units. For negative numbers, rounds away from zero.
Returns the smallest integer not less than `x`. Preserves units.
Discards the fractional part of `x`, leaving only the integer portion. Preserves units. Same as `floor` for positive `x`, `ceiling` for negative `x`.
Computes `x mod y`, i.e., the remainder after dividing `x` by `y`. Sign of the result follows `x`.
Returns the largest positive integer that divides every argument exactly. Accepts two or more arguments. Vector/matrix arguments are flattened element-wise first.

Parameters.Name: values
Parameters.Description: Two or more integers, vectors, or matrices

Function.Documentation: Returns the smallest positive integer that is a multiple of every argument. Accepts two or more arguments. Vector/matrix arguments are flattened element-wise first.

Parameters.Name: values
Parameters.Description: Two or more integers, vectors, or matrices

Function.Documentation: Returns `n!` = 1·2·3·…·n, the product of all positive integers up to `n`. The argument must be a dimensionless integer in the range 0 to 170; larger values overflow. Equivalent to the postfix `!` operator.

Function.Description: Real part of a complex number
Function.Documentation: Returns the real part of `z`. For a real input, returns `z` unchanged.

Function.Description: Imaginary part of a complex number
Function.Documentation: Returns the imaginary part of `z` as a real scalar. For a real input, returns 0.
Returns |z|. For a real number, the unsigned magnitude. For a complex number, `sqrt(re² + im²)`. Element-wise on vectors and matrices.

Function.Description: Phase angle of a complex number
Function.Documentation: Returns the argument (phase angle) of `z`, equivalent to `atan2(im(z); re(z))`. Result is in the current angle unit.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Angle in the current angle unit

Function.Documentation: Returns the complex conjugate of `z`, i.e., flips the sign of the imaginary part. For real input, returns `z` unchanged.

Function.Description: Minimum of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Returns the smallest value among all arguments. Vector/matrix arguments are flattened element-wise before comparison.
Returns the smallest element of `v`.
Returns the smallest element of `M` across all rows and columns.

Function.Description: Maximum of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Returns the largest value among all arguments. Vector/matrix arguments are flattened element-wise before comparison.
Returns the largest element of `v`.
Returns the largest element of `M` across all rows and columns.

Function.Description: Sum of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Adds every element of every argument. Vector/matrix arguments are flattened first.

Function.Description: Sum of all elements in a vector
Function.Documentation: Adds every element of `v` and returns the result.

Function.Description: Sum of all elements in a matrix
Function.Documentation: Adds every element of `M` (across rows and columns) and returns the result.

Function.Description: Sum of squares of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Sums `xᵢ²` over all arguments. Useful for variance/energy calculations.

Function.Description: Sum of squares of all elements in a vector
Function.Documentation: Returns Σ vᵢ². Equivalent to `v · v` (dot product with itself).

Function.Description: Sum of squares of all elements in a matrix
Function.Documentation: Returns Σ Mᵢⱼ² over the entire matrix (Frobenius norm squared).

Function.Description: Square root of sum of squares of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Computes `sqrt(Σ xᵢ²)`. Common in engineering for combining orthogonal components (e.g., load cases, modal responses).

Function.Description: Square root of sum of squares of all elements in a vector
Function.Documentation: Returns the Euclidean norm `sqrt(Σ vᵢ²)` of the vector.

Function.Description: Square root of sum of squares of all elements in a matrix
Function.Documentation: Returns the Frobenius norm `sqrt(Σ Mᵢⱼ²)` of the matrix.

Function.Description: Arithmetic mean of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Returns `(Σ xᵢ) / n`, where `n` is the total element count after flattening vector/matrix arguments.

Function.Description: Arithmetic mean of all elements in a vector
Function.Documentation: Returns `sum(v) / length(v)`.

Function.Description: Arithmetic mean of all elements in a matrix
Function.Documentation: Returns the sum of all elements divided by the total number of elements (rows × cols).

Function.Description: Product of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Multiplies every element of every argument together. Returns 1 for an empty input list.

Function.Description: Product of all elements in a vector
Function.Documentation: Returns Π vᵢ over the elements of `v`.

Function.Description: Product of all elements in a matrix
Function.Documentation: Returns Π Mᵢⱼ over the entire matrix.

Function.Description: Geometric mean of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: Returns the n-th root of the product of all `n` values: `(Π xᵢ)^(1/n)`. All arguments must be positive.

Function.Description: Geometric mean of all elements in a vector
Function.Documentation: Returns `(Π vᵢ)^(1/n)` where `n = length(v)`. All elements must be positive.

Function.Description: Geometric mean of all elements in a matrix
Function.Documentation: Returns `(Π Mᵢⱼ)^(1/n)` over all `n = rows × cols` elements. All elements must be positive.

Function.Description: Median of multiple values (scalars, vectors, or matrices)
Function.Documentation: The middle value of all elements after flattening and sorting; the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Has the unit of the first value.

Function.Description: Sample standard deviation (n - 1) of multiple values
Function.Documentation: `sqrt(Σ(xᵢ - x̄)² / (n - 1))` over all elements. Needs at least two values. Has the unit of the first value.

Function.Description: Population standard deviation (n) of multiple values
Function.Documentation: `sqrt(Σ(xᵢ - x̄)² / n)` over all elements. Has the unit of the first value.
`Σ(xᵢ - x̄)² / (n - 1)` over all elements. Needs at least two values. Has the square of the unit of the first value.
`Σ(xᵢ - x̄)² / n` over all elements. Has the square of the unit of the first value.

Function.Description: Returns the n-th element from a list of scalars
Function.Documentation: Picks the `n`-th argument (1-based) from the variadic list. Errors if `n` is out of range.

Function.Description: Returns the n-th element from a vector
Function.Documentation: Returns `v[n]` (1-based). Errors if `n` is out of range. To take multiple elements, use `extractRows`/`vec_slice`.

Function.Description: Returns the n-th element from a matrix
Function.Documentation: The matrix is linearized into a vector (row by row) and `M[n]` (1-based) is returned. Errors if `n` is out of range.

Function.Description: Linear interpolation with scalar data pairs
Function.Documentation: Performs piecewise linear interpolation at `x` over the data pairs `(x1, y1), (x2, y2), …`. Pairs must be sorted by `x` ascending.

Function.Description: Linear interpolation with x and y vectors
Function.Documentation: Performs piecewise linear interpolation at `x` using parallel `xData` and `yData` vectors. `xData` must be sorted ascending and have the same length as `yData`.

Function.Description: Linear interpolation over a linearized matrix
Function.Documentation: The matrix is linearized into a vector (row by row) and used as the data pairs `(x1, y1), (x2, y2), …` for piecewise linear interpolation at `x`.

Function.Description: Hermite spline interpolation with scalar data pairs
Function.Documentation: Performs smooth Hermite cubic spline interpolation at `x` over the data pairs. Smoother than `line` but more expensive.

Function.Description: Hermite spline interpolation with x and y vectors
Function.Documentation: Performs smooth Hermite cubic spline interpolation at `x` using parallel `xData` and `yData` vectors. `xData` must be sorted ascending.

Function.Description: Hermite spline interpolation over a linearized matrix
Function.Documentation: The matrix is linearized into a vector (row by row) and used as the data pairs for smooth Hermite cubic spline interpolation at `x`.
Returns `value-if-true` when `cond` is non-zero, otherwise `value-if-false`. Both branches are evaluated.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Same type as the chosen branch

Function.Documentation: Evaluates conditions in order and returns the value paired with the first true condition. The final unpaired argument is the default returned when no condition matches.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Same type as the matched value

Parameters.Name: pairs
Parameters.Description: Condition/value pairs followed by default value

Function.Documentation: Returns 1 if `x` is 0, otherwise 0. Use with comparisons and the boolean `and`/`or` family.

Function.Description: Logical AND of multiple boolean values
Function.Documentation: Returns 1 if every argument is non-zero, otherwise 0. Accepts two or more arguments. Note: this is **not** short-circuit - all arguments are evaluated.

Function.Description: Logical OR of multiple boolean values
Function.Documentation: Returns 1 if any argument is non-zero, otherwise 0. Accepts two or more arguments. Not short-circuit - all arguments are evaluated.

Function.Description: Logical XOR of multiple boolean values
Function.Documentation: Returns 1 if an odd number of arguments are non-zero, otherwise 0. Accepts two or more arguments.
Returns -1 for negative `x`, 0 for `x = 0`, and 1 for positive `x`. Strips units.
Returns a uniformly distributed random scalar from 0 to x. With no argument, returns a value from 0 to 1. Re-evaluating the document re-rolls the value.
Function.Example: random(100)  ' random integer-ish value from 0 to 100

Function.Description: Gets the units of x (returns 1 if unitless)
Function.Documentation: Extracts the unit dimension of `x` as a value of magnitude 1. Useful for stripping the numeric part: `x / getunits(x)` gives the magnitude.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Scalar with the same units as x, magnitude 1

Function.Description: Sets the units to a scalar, vector, or matrix
Function.Documentation: Reinterprets `x` as having the units of `u` (without numerical conversion). To convert between compatible units, use the `|` operator instead.
Function.ReturnTypeDescription: Same shape as x, with units of u

Function.Description: Clears the units from a scalar, vector, or matrix
Function.Documentation: Strips units from `x`, returning a dimensionless value with the same magnitude. Useful before passing to functions that require dimensionless input.

Converts a vector or matrix to a high-performance internal representation (single-precision, contiguous storage). Use for large numerical workloads where memory and speed matter; precision is reduced.

Function.Description: Checks if the type is high-performance
Function.Documentation: Returns 1 if `x` is stored in the high-performance representation (see `hp`), otherwise 0.

Returns the time in seconds elapsed since the calculation started. The argument is a value the timer depends on, so it is evaluated after that value; pass the expression whose runtime you want to measure.
Function.Example: timer(x)  ' seconds elapsed up to the evaluation of x

Function.Documentation: Returns a smooth escape-time value for the point `(x, y)` in the complex plane, used to render the Mandelbrot set. Points that belong to the set (do not escape) return `Undefined`. The result carries the units of `x`.

VectorFunction.Description: Creates an empty vector with length n
VectorFunction.Documentation: Allocates a new vector of length `n` with all elements initialized to 0. Use indexed assignment to populate it.

VectorFunction.Description: Creates an empty high-performance vector with length n
VectorFunction.Documentation: Like `vector(n)` but uses the high-performance representation (single-precision, contiguous storage). See `hp` for tradeoffs.

VectorFunction.Description: Creates a vector with values from x1 to xn with step s
VectorFunction.Documentation: Generates a sequence starting at `x1`, ending at or before `xn`, with step `s` (defaults to 1). Step may be negative for descending sequences.

VectorFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance vector from a range
VectorFunction.Documentation: Like `range(x1; xn; s)` but returns the high-performance vector representation.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns the length of the vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the allocated length of `v` (number of element slots). For the index of the last non-zero element, use `size`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns the actual size (index of last non-zero element)
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the index (1-based) of the last non-zero element of `v`. For a fully populated vector this equals `len(v)`. Useful for trimming trailing zeros.

VectorFunction.Description: Sets a new length for the vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `v` with length `n`. Truncates if `n < len(v)`, pads with zeros if `n > len(v)`.

VectorFunction.Description: Fills the vector with a value
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `v` with every element replaced by `x`. Length is preserved.

VectorFunction.Description: Creates a vector by joining matrices, vectors, and scalars
VectorFunction.Documentation: Concatenates all arguments into a single vector. Matrices are flattened in row-major order; scalars are appended as single elements.

Parameters.Name: items
Parameters.Description: Matrices, vectors, and scalars to join

VectorFunction.Description: Returns part of vector bounded by indexes i1 and i2
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the sub-vector `v[i1..i2]` (1-based, inclusive). Errors if indices are out of range or `i1 > i2`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns the first n elements of the vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Equivalent to `slice(v; 1; n)`. Returns the leading `n` elements of `v`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns the last n elements of the vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the trailing `n` elements of `v`, in their original order.

VectorFunction.Description: Extracts elements from v whose indexes are in i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns a new vector containing `v[i₁], v[i₂], …` in the order given by `i`. Indices may repeat to duplicate elements.

VectorFunction.Description: Sorts the vector in ascending order
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `v` with elements sorted in ascending order. For descending order use `rsort`. To get the sort permutation use `order`.

VectorFunction.Description: Sorts the vector in descending order
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `v` with elements sorted in descending order.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes in ascending order by element values
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the permutation `p` such that `v[p₁] ≤ v[p₂] ≤ …`. Use with `extract(v; order(v))` to sort while keeping a parallel vector aligned.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes in descending order by element values
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the permutation that sorts `v` in descending order. Inverse-direction counterpart to `order`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns vector with elements in reverse order
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `v` with element order flipped. Length is preserved.

VectorFunction.Description: Counts elements equal to x starting from index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Counts how many elements of `v` (from index `i` to the end) equal `x`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns index of first element equal to x starting from i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Linear search. Returns the 1-based index of the first occurrence of `x` in `v` at or after position `i`, or 0 if not found.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes of elements equal to x after index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns a vector of all 1-based indices ≥ `i` where `v[k] == x`. Empty result if none match. Same as `find_eq`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes of elements = x after index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns indices where `v[k] == x` for `k ≥ i`. Same as `find`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes of elements != x after index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns indices where `v[k] ≠ x` for `k ≥ i`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes of elements < x after index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns indices where `v[k] < x` for `k ≥ i`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes of elements <= x after index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns indices where `v[k] ≤ x` for `k ≥ i`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes of elements > x after index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns indices where `v[k] > x` for `k ≥ i`.

VectorFunction.Description: Returns indexes of elements >= x after index i
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns indices where `v[k] ≥ x` for `k ≥ i`.

VectorFunction.Description: Elements of a where corresponding elements of b equal x
VectorFunction.Documentation: For every position `k` where `b[k] == x`, returns `a[k]`. `a` and `b` must have the same length. Same as `lookup_eq`.

VectorFunction.Description: Elements of a where b elements = x
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `a[k]` for every `k` where `b[k] == x`. Same as `lookup`.

VectorFunction.Description: Elements of a where b elements != x
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `a[k]` for every `k` where `b[k] ≠ x`.

VectorFunction.Description: Elements of a where b elements < x
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `a[k]` for every `k` where `b[k] < x`.

VectorFunction.Description: Elements of a where b elements <= x
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `a[k]` for every `k` where `b[k] ≤ x`.

VectorFunction.Description: Elements of a where b elements > x
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `a[k]` for every `k` where `b[k] > x`.

VectorFunction.Description: Elements of a where b elements >= x
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `a[k]` for every `k` where `b[k] ≥ x`.

VectorFunction.Description: L2 (Euclidean) norm of vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Computes `sqrt(Σ vᵢ²)`, the Euclidean (L2) norm. Same as `norm_2` and `norm_e`.

VectorFunction.Description: L1 (Manhattan) norm of vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Computes `Σ |vᵢ|`, the L1 (taxicab) norm. Less sensitive to outliers than L2.

VectorFunction.Description: L2 (Euclidean) norm of vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Computes `sqrt(Σ vᵢ²)`, the Euclidean norm. Alias of `norm`.

VectorFunction.Description: L2 (Euclidean) norm of vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Alias of `norm` / `norm_2`.

VectorFunction.Description: Lp norm of vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Computes `(Σ |vᵢ|^p)^(1/p)` for arbitrary `p ≥ 1`. With `p = 1` reduces to `norm_1`, with `p = 2` to `norm_2`.

VectorFunction.Description: L-infinity norm of vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `max(|vᵢ|)` - the largest absolute element. Limit of `norm_p` as `p → ∞`.

VectorFunction.Description: Normalized vector (with L2 norm = 1)
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `v / norm(v)`, a vector pointing in the same direction with unit length. Errors if `v` is the zero vector.

VectorFunction.Description: Running sum of a vector
VectorFunction.Documentation: Element `k` of the result is `v₁ + ... + vₖ`. Same length and unit as `v`.

VectorFunction.Description: Discrete convolution of two vectors
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the full convolution, `len(a) + len(b) - 1` elements: the coefficients of the product of two polynomials. The unit is the product of the two units.

VectorFunction.Description: Vector of n equally spaced values from a to b
VectorFunction.Documentation: Both end points are included. With `n = 1` the result is `[a]`. The unit is that of `a`.

VectorFunction.Description: Least-squares polynomial fit
VectorFunction.Documentation: Fits `y = c₁ + c₂·x + ... + cₙ₊₁·xⁿ` to the points and returns the coefficients in ascending order `[c₁; c₂; ...]` (n + 1 elements). Needs at least n + 1 points and distinct x values. Coefficient k carries the unit `y / x^(k-1)`.

VectorFunction.Description: Linear interpolation in a table
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the value of `y` at `x` by linear interpolation between the points (`xs`, `ys`). `xs` must be strictly increasing. A value outside the table is an error. The unit is that of `ys`; `x` is converted to the unit of `xs`.

VectorFunction.Description: Linear interpolation in a table, continued outside it
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the value of `y` at `x` by linear interpolation between the points (`xs`, `ys`), like `interp`. Outside the table the first or last segment is continued as a straight line instead of being an error. `xs` must be strictly increasing and the table needs two points. The unit is that of `ys`; `x` is converted to the unit of `xs`.

VectorFunction.Description: Scalar (dot) product of two vectors
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns `Σ aᵢ · bᵢ`. Vectors must have the same length. Equals `|a| · |b| · cos(θ)` for the angle `θ` between them.

VectorFunction.Description: Cross product of two vectors (length 2 or 3)
VectorFunction.Documentation: Returns the cross product `a × b`. For 3-vectors, yields a vector perpendicular to both. For 2-vectors, returns the scalar z-component.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates an empty matrix with dimensions m x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Allocates a new `m × n` matrix with all elements initialized to 0. Use indexed assignment to populate it.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates an identity matrix with dimensions n x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `n × n` identity matrix `I` (1s on the diagonal, 0s elsewhere).

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a diagonal matrix n x n filled with value d
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns an `n × n` matrix with `d` on the main diagonal and 0 elsewhere. For `d = 1` use `identity(n)` instead.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a column matrix m x 1 filled with value c
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns an `m × 1` column matrix with every element equal to `c`. For row vectors use `vec2row`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates an upper triangular matrix n x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns an `n × n` matrix that stores only the upper triangle (entries `Mᵢⱼ` with `j ≥ i`). Lower-triangle entries are implicitly zero.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a lower triangular matrix n x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns an `n × n` matrix that stores only the lower triangle (entries `Mᵢⱼ` with `j ≤ i`).

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a symmetric matrix n x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns an `n × n` matrix with the symmetric storage layout: assigning `M[i; j]` automatically mirrors to `M[j; i]`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance matrix m x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Like `matrix(m; n)` but uses the high-performance representation (single-precision, contiguous storage). See `hp` for tradeoffs.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance identity matrix n x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: High-performance variant of `identity(n)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance diagonal matrix n x n
MatrixFunction.Documentation: High-performance variant of `diagonal(n; d)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance column matrix m x 1
MatrixFunction.Documentation: High-performance variant of `column(m; c)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance upper triangular matrix
MatrixFunction.Documentation: High-performance variant of `utriang(n)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance lower triangular matrix
MatrixFunction.Documentation: High-performance variant of `ltriang(n)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a high-performance symmetric matrix
MatrixFunction.Documentation: High-performance variant of `symmetric(n)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a diagonal matrix from vector elements
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns an `n × n` matrix where `M[i; i] = v[i]` and all off-diagonal entries are 0. Inverse is `diag2vec`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a row matrix from vector elements
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a `1 × n` row matrix containing the elements of `v`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a column matrix from vector elements
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns an `n × 1` column matrix containing the elements of `v`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a matrix by joining column vectors
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Treats each argument as a column and stacks them side by side. All vectors must have the same length.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a matrix by joining row vectors
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Treats each argument as a row and stacks them top to bottom. All vectors must have the same length.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a matrix by appending matrices side by side
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Concatenates matrices horizontally. All matrices must have the same number of rows. A vector argument is treated as a single column.

MatrixFunction.Description: Creates a matrix by stacking matrices vertically
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Concatenates matrices vertically. All matrices must have the same number of columns. A vector argument is treated as an n×1 column matrix, so it contributes rows of length 1 that are zero-padded to the width of the result.

MatrixFunction.Description: Number of rows in matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the row count of `M`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Number of columns in matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the column count of `M`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Sets new dimensions m and n for matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `M` reshaped to `m × n`. Existing entries within the new bounds are preserved; new cells are zero-filled.

MatrixFunction.Description: Fills the matrix M with value x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `M` with every element replaced by `x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Fills the i-th row of matrix M with value x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `M` with row `i` set to `x` in every column.

MatrixFunction.Description: Fills the j-th column of matrix M with value x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `M` with column `j` set to `x` in every row.

MatrixFunction.Description: Copies all elements from A to B starting at indexes i, j
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `B` with the elements of `A` written into the block starting at row `i`, column `j`. Errors if `A` would extend past the bounds of `B`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Adds elements from A to B starting at indexes i, j
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a copy of `B` with `A`'s elements added (rather than overwritten) into the block at `(i, j)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Extracts the i-th row of matrix M as a vector
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `i`-th row of `M` as a vector of length `n_cols(M)`. A vector is treated as an n×1 column matrix, so `row` yields a single element.

MatrixFunction.Description: Extracts the j-th column of matrix M as a vector
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `j`-th column of `M` as a vector of length `n_rows(M)`. A vector is treated as an n×1 column matrix, so `col(v; 1)` returns the vector itself.

MatrixFunction.Description: Extracts rows from M whose indexes are in vector i
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a new matrix with the rows of `M` selected and reordered by the indices in `i`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Extracts columns from M whose indexes are in vector j
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a new matrix with the columns of `M` selected and reordered by the indices in `j`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Extracts diagonal elements of matrix M to a vector
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the main diagonal `[M[1;1], M[2;2], …, M[k;k]]` where `k = min(rows, cols)`. Inverse is `vec2diag`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Extracts submatrix bounded by rows i1-i2 and columns j1-j2
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the rectangular block of `M` from `(i1, j1)` to `(i2, j2)` inclusive (1-based bounds).

MatrixFunction.Description: Sorts columns based on values in row i (ascending)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Reorders the columns of `M` so that row `i` is in ascending order. All columns move together as units.

MatrixFunction.Description: Sorts columns based on values in row i (descending)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Reorders the columns of `M` so that row `i` is in descending order.

MatrixFunction.Description: Sorts rows based on values in column j (ascending)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Reorders the rows of `M` so that column `j` is in ascending order.

MatrixFunction.Description: Sorts rows based on values in column j (descending)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Reorders the rows of `M` so that column `j` is in descending order.

MatrixFunction.Description: Column indexes in ascending order by row i values
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the permutation of column indices that would sort row `i` ascending. Use `extract_cols` to apply it.

MatrixFunction.Description: Column indexes in descending order by row i values
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the permutation of column indices that would sort row `i` descending.

MatrixFunction.Description: Row indexes in ascending order by column j values
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the permutation of row indices that would sort column `j` ascending.

MatrixFunction.Description: Row indexes in descending order by column j values
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the permutation of row indices that would sort column `j` descending.

MatrixFunction.Description: Number of occurrences of value x in matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the count of elements of `M` equal to `x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Vector with indexes of first occurrence of x starting from i, j
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Searches `M` row-by-row from `(i, j)` for the first occurrence of `x` and returns `[row; col]`. Returns `[0; 0]` if not found.

MatrixFunction.Description: Indexes of all elements in M equal to x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a 2-row matrix where each column is `[row; col]` of an element equal to `x`. Same as `mfind_eq`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Indexes of elements = x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `[row; col]` indices of every element equal to `x`. Same as `mfind`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Indexes of elements != x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `[row; col]` indices of every element not equal to `x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Indexes of elements < x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `[row; col]` indices of every element less than `x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Indexes of elements <= x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `[row; col]` indices of every element ≤ `x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Indexes of elements > x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `[row; col]` indices of every element greater than `x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Indexes of elements >= x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the `[row; col]` indices of every element ≥ `x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from row i2 where row i1 elements = x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: For every column `k` where `M[i1; k] == x`, returns `M[i2; k]`. Useful for looking up values across a header row. Same as `hlookup_eq`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from row i2 where row i1 = x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Same as `hlookup`. Returns `M[i2; k]` for each `k` where `M[i1; k] == x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from row i2 where row i1 != x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[i2; k]` for each `k` where `M[i1; k] ≠ x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from row i2 where row i1 < x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[i2; k]` for each `k` where `M[i1; k] < x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from row i2 where row i1 <= x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[i2; k]` for each `k` where `M[i1; k] ≤ x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from row i2 where row i1 > x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[i2; k]` for each `k` where `M[i1; k] > x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from row i2 where row i1 >= x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[i2; k]` for each `k` where `M[i1; k] ≥ x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from column j2 where column j1 = x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: For every row `k` where `M[k; j1] == x`, returns `M[k; j2]`. The matrix-column analog of Excel's VLOOKUP.
MatrixFunction.Example: vlookup(M; 'A'; 1; 2)  ' all column-2 values where column 1 contains 'A'

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from column j2 where column j1 = x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Same as `vlookup`. Returns `M[k; j2]` for each `k` where `M[k; j1] == x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from column j2 where column j1 != x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[k; j2]` for each `k` where `M[k; j1] ≠ x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from column j2 where column j1 < x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[k; j2]` for each `k` where `M[k; j1] < x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from column j2 where column j1 <= x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[k; j2]` for each `k` where `M[k; j1] ≤ x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from column j2 where column j1 > x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[k; j2]` for each `k` where `M[k; j1] > x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Values from column j2 where column j1 >= x
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[k; j2]` for each `k` where `M[k; j1] ≥ x`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Hadamard (element-wise) product of matrices A and B
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the element-wise product `Cᵢⱼ = Aᵢⱼ · Bᵢⱼ`. `A` and `B` must have the same shape. A vector argument is treated as an n×1 column matrix.

MatrixFunction.Description: Frobenius product of matrices A and B
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `Σ Aᵢⱼ · Bᵢⱼ` - the matrix analog of the dot product. Requires matching shapes.

MatrixFunction.Description: Kronecker product of matrices A and B
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the block-tensor product `A ⊗ B`. If `A` is `m × n` and `B` is `p × q`, the result is `(m·p) × (n·q)`.

MatrixFunction.Description: L2 norm of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the spectral (largest singular value) norm. Same as `mnorm_2`.

MatrixFunction.Description: L1 norm of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the maximum absolute column sum: `max_j Σᵢ |Mᵢⱼ|`.

MatrixFunction.Description: L2 norm of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the spectral norm - the largest singular value of `M`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Frobenius norm of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `sqrt(Σ Mᵢⱼ²)` - the entrywise L2 norm.

MatrixFunction.Description: L-infinity norm of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the maximum absolute row sum: `max_i Σⱼ |Mᵢⱼ|`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Condition number based on L2 norm
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `‖M‖₂ · ‖M⁻¹‖₂`. A large condition number indicates an ill-conditioned matrix where small input perturbations cause large output changes. Same as `cond_2`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Condition number based on L1 norm
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `‖M‖₁ · ‖M⁻¹‖₁`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Condition number based on L2 norm
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `‖M‖₂ · ‖M⁻¹‖₂` - the ratio of the largest to smallest singular value.

MatrixFunction.Description: Condition number based on Frobenius norm
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `‖M‖_F · ‖M⁻¹‖_F`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Condition number based on L-infinity norm
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `‖M‖_∞ · ‖M⁻¹‖_∞`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Determinant of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Computes `det(M)`. `M` must be square. Returns 0 for singular matrices (within floating-point tolerance).

MatrixFunction.Description: Rank of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the rank of `M` - the number of linearly independent rows/columns. Computed via SVD.

MatrixFunction.Description: Trace of matrix M (sum of diagonal elements)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `Σ Mᵢᵢ`. `M` must be square.

MatrixFunction.Description: Transpose of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M^T` - rows become columns and vice versa. An `m × n` matrix becomes `n × m`. A vector is treated as an n×1 column matrix, so its transpose is a 1×n row matrix.

MatrixFunction.Description: Adjugate of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `adj(M)` - the transpose of the cofactor matrix. Satisfies `M · adj(M) = det(M) · I`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Cofactor matrix of M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the matrix of signed minors of `M`. The transpose of this is the adjugate (`adj`).

MatrixFunction.Description: Real roots of a polynomial
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the real roots of the polynomial whose coefficients are in vector `v`, constant term first (`v.1 + v.2*x + v.3*x^2 + ...`), in ascending order. Complex roots are left out.

MatrixFunction.Description: First ne eigenvalues of matrix M (or all if omitted)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the eigenvalues of the square matrix `M` as a vector, in ascending order. `ne > 0` keeps the first `ne`; a negative `ne` keeps the `|ne|` largest, in descending order. `M` can be symmetric or not; a matrix with complex eigenvalues is refused (use `ceigenvals`). Units of `M` carry over.

MatrixFunction.Description: First ne eigenvectors of matrix M (or all if omitted)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns a matrix with one unit eigenvector per row, in the order of `eigenvals(M; ne)`. `M` can be symmetric or not; a matrix with complex eigenvalues is refused (use `ceigenvecs`).

MatrixFunction.Description: First ne eigenvalues and eigenvectors (or all if omitted)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns one row per eigenpair: the eigenvalue in column 1 and its eigenvector in the remaining columns. Cheaper than calling `eigenvals` and `eigenvecs` separately.

MatrixFunction.Description: Complex eigenvalues of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns all eigenvalues of the square matrix `M`, including complex ones, as a 2 × n matrix: real parts in row 1, imaginary parts in row 2 (the `fft` layout). Sorted by real part, then imaginary part. Eigenvalue k is `C.(1; k) + C.(2; k)*1i`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Complex eigenvectors of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the unit eigenvectors of the square matrix `M`, including complex ones, as a 2n × n matrix: eigenvector k is row 2k - 1 (real parts) plus row 2k (imaginary parts), in the order of `ceigenvals(M)`.
MatrixFunction.ReturnTypeDescription: Matrix 2n × n (real and imaginary rows per eigenvector)

MatrixFunction.Description: Cholesky decomposition of symmetric positive-definite matrix
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the lower-triangular factor `L` such that `M = L · L^T`. `M` must be symmetric and positive-definite, otherwise an error is raised.

MatrixFunction.Description: LU decomposition of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the combined `L` (below diagonal) + `U` (above and on diagonal) factors with partial pivoting.

MatrixFunction.Description: QR decomposition of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns the combined Q + R factors. `Q` is orthogonal, `R` is upper-triangular, and `M = Q · R`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Singular value decomposition of M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `U`, `Σ`, and `Vᵀ` packed into a single matrix such that `M = U · Σ · Vᵀ`. Singular values are in descending order on the diagonal of `Σ`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Inverse of matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M⁻¹` such that `M · M⁻¹ = I`. Errors for singular matrices. For solving `Ax = b`, prefer `lsolve(A; b)` over `inverse(A) · b`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Solves Ax = b using LDLT (symmetric) or LU decomposition
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Solves the linear system `A · x = b` for `x`. Automatically picks LDLT for symmetric `A` and LU otherwise.

MatrixFunction.Description: Solves Ax = b using Cholesky decomposition
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Solves `A · x = b` using Cholesky factorization. Faster than `lsolve` but requires `A` to be symmetric and positive-definite.

MatrixFunction.Description: Solves Ax = b using preconditioned conjugate gradient
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Iterative solver for very large symmetric positive-definite systems. `A` should be in the high-performance representation.

MatrixFunction.Description: Solves AX = B using LDLT or LU decomposition
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Solves the matrix system `A · X = B` for `X` (multiple right-hand sides packed as columns of `B`).

MatrixFunction.Description: Solves AX = B using Cholesky decomposition
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Cholesky-based variant of `msolve`. `A` must be symmetric positive-definite.

MatrixFunction.Description: Solves AX = B using preconditioned conjugate gradient
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Iterative matrix-system solver. `A` should be in the HP representation; suitable for very large symmetric positive-definite systems.

MatrixFunction.Description: Fast Fourier transform (1 row for real, 2 for complex)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Computes the discrete Fourier transform. Pass a 1-row matrix for real input or a 2-row matrix (real, imaginary) for complex input. Output is always a 2-row complex matrix.

MatrixFunction.Description: Inverse Fourier transform (1 row for real, 2 for complex)
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Computes the inverse discrete Fourier transform. Inverse of `fft`.

MatrixFunction.Description: Returns element of matrix M at indexes x and y
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Returns `M[x; y]` (1-based). Equivalent to `M[x; y]` in expression syntax.

MatrixFunction.Description: Double linear interpolation from matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Performs bilinear interpolation at fractional indices `(x, y)` using the values of `M`. Useful for 2-D table lookups.

MatrixFunction.Description: Double Hermite spline interpolation from matrix M
MatrixFunction.Documentation: Performs smooth bicubic Hermite spline interpolation at `(x, y)` using `M` as the data table. Smoother than `line` but more expensive.

Css.Label: Report Fonts
Css.Description: Override the report font family and sizes
Css.Documentation:
Restyles the rendered output, seeded with the template's stock sizes so it is a no-op until a number is changed.

`body` is the master size control: `.eq` has no size of its own and inherits it, and `.eq sub`, `.eq small` and `.nary` are percentages that follow it. The `pt` entries do not - variable names, units, matrix cells and input fields are fixed in the template and have to be moved separately. Headings are sized in `em` off `body`, so they already scale and are not listed.

The family is set to Georgia Pro, which is not bundled and must be installed on the machine viewing the report.

Css.Label: Report Table
Css.Documentation:
For tables written by hand with `class="bordered"` - the *HTML Table* snippet inserts the skeleton. Seeded with the template's stock values, so it is a no-op until a number is changed.

The class is not decoration only: Word export reads it to decide whether the table keeps its borders, so dropping it changes the `.docx` as well as the report.

Markdown tables are a separate case - Markdig gives them no class, so they are reached through `thead`/`tbody` instead. See *Markdown Table*.

Css.Label: UI Controls - All
Css.Description: Style sheet covering every #UI control type
Css.Documentation:
One rule per control base class, as a starting point.

| Type | Element | Base class |
|---|---|---|
| `entry` | `<input type="text">` | `calcpad-ui-input` |
| `dropdown` | `<select>` | `calcpad-ui-dropdown` |
| `radio` | `<span>` | `calcpad-ui-radio`, labels `calcpad-ui-radio-label` |
| `checkbox` | `<input type="checkbox">` | `calcpad-ui-checkbox` |
| `datagrid` | `<div>` | `calcpad-ui-datagrid` |

Pair it with a `style` class on the directive, which applies in Input mode only:

`#UI {"style": "highlight"} depth = 2m`

Combine the base class with your own so the rule only hits the controls you marked - `.calcpad-ui-input.highlight`, not `.highlight`. Several classes can be listed at once: `"style": "highlight wide"`.

`p.boxed` is for `reportStyle`, which lands on the line's paragraph everywhere the line is not a control - Preview, Report and every export but the input form.

Css.Label: UI Entry Box
Css.Documentation:
Targets `<input type="text">` controls.

Pair it with a `style` class on the directive, which applies in Input mode only:

`#UI {"style": "highlight"} depth = 2m`

Combine the base class with your own so the rule only hits the controls you marked - `.calcpad-ui-input.highlight`, not `.highlight`. Several classes can be listed at once: `"style": "highlight wide"`.

Css.Label: UI Radio Group
Css.Documentation:
The class lands on the wrapping `<span>`; each button's `<label>` carries `calcpad-ui-radio-label`, so spacing is set through a descendant selector.

`#UI {"type": "radio", "style": "compact", "keys": ["Steel", "Concrete"], "values": ["200GPa", "25GPa"]} E = 200GPa`

Css.Label: UI Datagrid
Css.Description: Style the container of an #UI datagrid
Css.Documentation:
The class reaches the grid's outer `<div>` only. A grid is a third-party widget, so its cells, headers and context menu are styled by a stylesheet that ships with the application, not from the document - see *Customizing the `#UI` Datagrid* in `DEVELOPER.md`. Column widths and overall grid size are set by the preview script and are not adjustable from CSS at all.

`#UI {"type": "datagrid", "style": "bordered"} T = [1; 2 | 3; 4]`

Css.Label: UI Report Line
Css.Description: Style a #UI line outside the input form
Css.Documentation:
For `reportStyle`, which is the counterpart to `style`: it lands on the element wrapping the line everywhere the line is *not* a control - Preview, Report and every export but the input form. That element is a paragraph, so target it as `p.boxed`.

`#UI {"reportStyle": "boxed"} P = 25kN`

Css.Label: Markdown Elements - All
Css.Documentation:
The report template styles headings, paragraphs and Calcpad's own output, but leaves most of what Markdown produces on browser defaults. This covers the lot.

| Markdown | Element |
|---|---|
| `> quote` | `blockquote > p` |
| fenced block | `pre > code.language-*` |
| `` `code` `` | `code` |
| `---` | `hr` |
| `- [x] item` | `ul.contains-task-list > li.task-list-item > input` |
| pipe table | `table > thead > th`, `tbody > td` |
| `++ins++`, `~~del~~` | `ins`, `del` |

Tables are reached through `thead`/`tbody`, which Calcpad's own tables never emit, so matrices and `#UI` datagrids are left alone.

Inside an `#html` or `#markdown` block, write the `<style>` element directly - no `'` quotes and no `#val` wrapper. Those are only needed in Calcpad mode, where an unquoted line is an expression.

Rules apply to the whole report, so a `.dark-theme` counterpart is needed for anything that sets a colour - see the template for the convention.
